The South Korean government had previously announced that cash investments worth 200 billion U.S. dollars, following the outcome of the Korea-U.S. tariff negotiations, would be restricted to projects with commercial rationality. Minister Kim clarified that the Alaska gas field project does not align with these standards.

When Rep. Bae Joon-young of the People Power Party asked, “Can we consider this outside the scope of our investable items?” Minister Kim replied, “That is the case for now.” He added, however, “Given aspects like gas security diversification, both domestic companies and the government are monitoring the project’s progress with interest.”

Earlier, U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick wrote on social media, SNS on the 30th of last month that out of the 350 billion U.S. dollars South Korea agreed to invest in the U.S., 200 billion U.S. dollars would be directed toward projects including the Alaska natural gas pipeline, energy infrastructure, critical minerals, advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI), and quantum computing within the U.S.
